records.question: What supply-chain risks did Apple list in its most recent annual report?
records.answer: In its fiscal year 2025 annual report, Apple listed several supply-chain risks, including reliance on a large, complex global supply chain where a majority of supplier facilities, manufacturing, and assembly sites are located outside the U.S. [1]. The company noted risks from single or limited sources for critical components, potential supply shortages, price increases, industry-wide shortages such as in semiconductors, and capacity constraints when utilizing new technologies [2][3][6]. Apple also highlighted vulnerabilities to natural disasters, extreme weather, geopolitical tensions, trade disputes, tariffs, public health issues, industrial accidents, and cyberattacks that can disrupt its supply chain and operations [1][2][4]. Additionally, outsourcing much of its manufacturing, transportation, and logistics reduces direct control over production and distribution, while changes or additions to the supply chain require considerable time, resources, and involve operational and regulatory risks [6].

records.question: Summarize all the rules in the fraud memo.
records.answer: The real-time card fraud rules effective from March 1, 2026, include Rule R-101 (Velocity), which declines the sixth and later card-not-present purchases within 10 minutes and texts the customer [6]. Rule R-104 (Geo-jump) declines the second of two card-present purchases more than 500 miles apart within 2 hours and places a soft block [6]. Rule R-110 (First foreign use) requires step-up verification in the app for a first-ever foreign purchase over $400 [6]. Rule R-117 (Merchant risk) holds purchases for analyst review up to 4 hours when the merchant is on the high-risk list and the amount is over $250 [6]. Rule R-122 (New-device spend) declines purchases over $1,000 within 24 hours of a new device enrolling and requires a call to Customer Care [6]. Rule R-130 (ATM pattern) blocks ATM access for 24 hours after 3 or more out-of-network ATM withdrawals in one day at different terminals [6].

records.question: What did Microsoft list as its main risks in its latest annual report?
records.answer: In its latest annual report, Microsoft listed intense competition across all markets for its products and services [1], strategic and competitive risks such as advertising, professional, marketplace, and gaming platform abuses [2], and business model challenges including cloud and AI services [5]. It also noted risks from global, regional, and local economic developments and changes in trade policies [3], as well as other digital safety abuses, geopolitical conditions, climate change [4], and risks to its investment portfolio and potential disruptions from catastrophic events [6].
